initial_analysis.mode: SIGNAL (wavelet sigma avg 4.9; pairs 0-3 sigma>2; pair4 sigma=1.8)

pair_level_statistics.note: wavelet HH-MAD sigma is a MAD high-pass scale, empirically ~0.5x the true additive sigma (calibrated on synthetic noise, see statistical_checks); direct residual std includes a small structured component

noise_6step_check.note: peeled_noise_check.py values on the un-stripped residual. The automated IMPULSE verdict is rejected (known FP). Calibration on a pure synthetic gaussian_RGB:1 residual (see statistical_checks) gives extreme_pct=53.2%, vm_slope=0.077, var_slope=-0.07, spatial_corr=0.34 even though the noise is i.i.d. Gaussian — so extreme_pct, vm_slope, var_slope and spatial_corr are non-discriminative under this metric implementation. rgb_ratio and cross_channel_corr remain usable.
noise_6step_check.diagnosis: Impulse excluded (run_full_analysis impulse_zero_ratio 0.04-0.21, far below the 0.85 impulse fingerprint; no salt-and-pepper pixels visible). Speckle/Poisson excluded: region-wise noise sigma is not monotonic in intensity (pair1 regions at mean 86/93/108/167 have sigma 20/27/17/11-25; pairs 2 and 4 similar), and var_slope is negative. YCrCb-style channel-correlated noise is favored: rgb_ratio >1.4 and cross_channel_corr >0.35 in 4/5 pairs, with per-channel sigma ordering varying by content (R<G<B in pair0/pair3, B high in pair1, flat in pair2). The residual is essentially i.i.d.-like at pixel scale (autocorr FWHM <1 px; spatial_corr ~= the 0.34 i.i.d. bias measured on a synthetic pure-noise residual).

estimator_calibration.note: Same estimator (run_full_analysis estimate_noise_sigma / verify_signals) applied to synthetic x_distortion noise on pair0/pair1 clean images; establishes scale and §B false-positive levels.
estimator_calibration.scale_factor: wavelet/Haar HH-MAD and DoG MAD both report ~0.5x the true additive sigma; the factor is identical for target and simulated, so verify_signals sigma-diff percentages remain valid. True target sigma ~= 2x reported wavelet sigma.
estimator_calibration.takeaway: §B extreme_pct ~50% and spatial_corr ~0.34 are formal artifacts of the metric, not evidence of impulse/spatially-correlated noise. Only rgb_ratio + cross_channel_corr discriminate noise type in this case.

coupling_analysis.noise_fakes_global: run_full_analysis on pure synthetic noise (RGB:1 and YCrCb:1) returns CONTRAST_strengthen + SATURATION flags identical to target pairs 0/2/3. This is direct proof that the target's global verdicts are noise artifacts on these flat patches; variance_ratio scales with noise level, not with a deterministic contrast step.
coupling_analysis.noise_masks_blur: gm_ratio is inflated 5-14x by noise and cannot indicate blur. The spectral slope direction is decisive: target spectrum is flatter than clean (ratio 0.24-0.41), whereas blur steepens it. Blur simulation on the lowest-noise pair lowers PSNR below the no-degradation baseline and CI=1/10.
coupling_analysis.noise_masks_compression: Noise attenuates block_boundary. Pair4 (lowest noise) shows block_boundary=1.1185 and the highest dct_zero_ratio 0.1125; pairs 0-3 show ~1.0. However, the mildest library JPEG (q=25) produces bb=6.58 and q=18 produces ~33, i.e. 6-30x the target's excess blockiness. A mild in-camera/high-quality JPEG (out-of-library quality) or SIDD GT processing is the only viable explanation; it is unverifiable and therefore excluded from the main pipeline.
coupling_analysis.clean_vs_target_offset: Target means are slightly darker than clean in pairs 0-2 (-1.0/-2.2/-3.7 to -9.1/-4.6/-10.9 per channel) with 2.9-6.9% of pixels clipped at 0. The offset is inconsistent across pairs and small relative to the noise sigma; it is consistent with clipping/ISP tone mapping in the real capture, not with a shared brightness step.
coupling_analysis.pipeline_order: Single stochastic step only. No deterministic steps supported, so order constraints do not apply.
coupling_analysis.real_data_signature: The residual's pixel-scale autocorrelation is white (FWHM <1 px) but its direct std is 1.6-1.8x the white-noise MAD scale, matching the same ratio measured on synthetic i.i.d. noise (2.0x with sampling variance). The residual is therefore dominated by pixel-scale random noise rather than low-frequency clean-GT structure. The magnitude varies 6x across pairs (true sigma ~3.7 to ~23), which is characteristic of real, signal/exposure-dependent sensor noise across SIDD crops, not a single synthetic additive severity applied to all five clean images.

hypothesis.thinking: Pair4 block_boundary=1.1185>1.1 (0%FP signal) + dct_zero_ratio=0.1125 (highest of 5 pairs). Signal mode chosen because target still has sigma~1.9 noise; block_boundary/dct are the physically valid discriminators on flat patches.

Severity scan rule: sev1 (mildest library JPEG, q=25) already produced block_boundary ~6x target (diff 489%). Test sev2 to confirm monotonic impossibility; if stronger is worse, x_distortion JPEG range cannot explain the mild 8x8 structure in pair4.

Blur control (decision-tree default gaussian). Pair4 has the lowest noise (sigma 1.8), so residual blur would be maximally visible; spectral_slope_ratio=0.35 (<1.08) and FFT anisotropy=0 argue against blur. Baseline clean-vs-target PSNR = 32.1 dB; a correct blur step should not lower PSNR below this.

iterations.agent_note: Tool auto-labelled ADJUST_SEVERITY because 31.75 dB falls in the 30-40 band, but the correct interpretation is REJECT: PSNR is below the no-degradation baseline (32.1 dB) and CI=1/10; blur adds error rather than explaining the target.

hypothesis.thinking: Global control: run_full_analysis flagged CONTRAST_strengthen on pair0, but its own FP flags fired and variance_ratio tracks noise magnitude across pairs. A true global step should reproduce mean_shift and variance_ratio.

Noise candidate per noise_prior: per-channel wavelet sigma R2.6/G5.2/B6.3 (ratio 2.4), cross_ch_corr=0.33, residual_intensity_corr=-0.12. YCrCb sev1 is the mildest YCrCb setting. Signal mode because sigma>2.
Cross-family control for pair0: rgb_ratio=1.82 favors YCrCb, but the target magnitude might be closer to the RGB grid. Test gaussian_RGB sev1.
Pair1 target wavelet sigma=11.6 (strongest of 5). Estimator calibration from pair0 sims: RGB sev1 measures 6.3 => RGB sev2 should measure ~12.6, within 20% of target.
Noise-family coverage. var_slope is negative on the residual and region-wise sigma is not monotonic in intensity, so Poisson is not signal-supported; control test.

iterations.agent_note: Scalar checks cannot distinguish Poisson from Gaussian at this magnitude; fingerprint evidence (var_slope, region-intensity relation) contradicts Poisson, so this remains a weak alternative only.

hypothesis.thinking: Noise-family coverage: speckle (multiplicative). Region-wise sigma does not scale with intensity, arguing against multiplicative noise; control test.
Pair2 is the channel-flat case (wavelet R8.5/G8.9/B8.9, ratio 1.05; peeled noise_prior predicted gaussian_RGB). Target sigma=8.77 lies between calibrated RGB sev1 (~6.3) and sev2 (~12.6).
Pair2 cross-family test after RGB1 WEAK. YCrCb1 is the only YCrCb step whose measured sigma can approach 8.8; channel-flat ratio argues against YCrCb, so this is a controlled falsification.
Mandatory severity scan after RGB1 WEAK on pair0 (target sigma 4.69 below calibrated RGB sev1=6.3). Upward scan expected to increase mismatch, documenting a below-library-floor target.
Pair4 target wavelet sigma=1.85 (lowest). Calibrated minimum library step RGB sev1 measures ~6.3, so this tests whether the case is below the x_distortion noise floor.

Type discrimination on pair1: target high-pass sigma R22.9/G19.0/B28.0 (G lowest, B highest, cross_ch=0.445). Calibrated sims: YCrCb sev1 yields R19.2-21.9/G14.2-16.2/B22.6-25.5 (same G-low/B-high pattern, cross_ch=0.148-0.28) vs RGB sev2 uniform 25.5 (cross_ch=0.005). Same scalar magnitude (target wavelet 11.6 vs sim 10.75) but YCrCb matches the channel/cross-channel fingerprint.

Complete the per-pair table for the leading pipeline. Pair3 wavelet sigma=2.84 (R1.5/G3.0/B4.1, ratio 2.8 chroma-heavy) is below the calibrated library floor; expected sigma mismatch documents out-of-range severity while the channel pattern still supports the YCrCb family.

psnr_ranking_note: Only the blur control was run in PSNR mode by design. All noise candidates were verified with verify_signals per SKILL (noise seed mismatch makes PSNR meaningless). Clean-vs-target PSNR on pair4 is 32.1 dB and is the no-degradation baseline against which blur's 31.75 dB is below baseline.

alternatives.evidence: verify_signals MATCH on pair1 (sigma + residual autocorr); contradicts the target's channel ratio (~1.5) and cross_channel_corr (0.445) because RGB is channel-flat. Keep as cross-family backup.
MATCH on the two scalar noise checks for pair1 only; var_slope is negative and region-wise sigma is not monotonic in intensity, so the Poisson fingerprint is contradicted. Low-quality alternative.

final_decision.rationale: Noise is present in all five pairs and is the only supported degradation. Blur, global contrast/brightness/saturation and library JPEG are excluded by direct simulation (blur below-baseline PSNR + CI 1/10; contrast 507% variance mismatch; JPEG 489-2858% blockiness overshoot). The noise is channel-correlated and chroma-heavy in 4/5 pairs (rgb_ratio 1.46-1.82, cross_ch 0.43-0.56) with a white pixel-scale residual; gaussian_YCrCb:1 reproduces pair1 exactly (sigma 7.4% off, same per-channel ordering) and pair2 approximately (23%), but it is 1.3-3.8x too strong for pairs 0/3 and ~5x too strong for pair4. The per-pair true noise sigma spans ~3.7-23 levels, below the x_distortion noise floor (minimum library step ~12.8 uniform / ~21.5 YCrCb RGB-equivalent) for 3/5 pairs. This pattern is characteristic of real, image-dependent SIDD sensor noise rather than one synthetic severity applied to all five clean images, so exact in-library reproduction is not possible; the pipeline above is the closest in-library proxy, exact for the strongest pair and an upper bound for the rest.

per_pair_fit.pair2: YCrCb:1 closest (23%); RGB:1 27%; true sigma on-grid gap (between sev1 and sev2)

per_pair_fit.pair4: YCrCb:1 far out of range (RGB:1 already 240% too strong); mild 8x8 blockiness present but library JPEG is 6-30x too strong

limitations: Real SIDD-style sensor noise is signal/exposure dependent and not exactly representable by i.i.d. additive x_distortion noise; the single library severity cannot cover the 6x magnitude spread across support pairs.

Noise subtype (YCrCb vs RGB) is supported by channel-ratio/cross-channel fingerprints, but verify_signals' noise checks only test scalar sigma and residual autocorrelation, which cannot confirm subtype.

Pair4's block_boundary=1.1185 may indicate a mild in-camera JPEG (quality far above q=25), but the library JPEG range is an order of magnitude too strong and the structure is absent in the other pairs; compression is therefore not predicted.
Global flags in run_full_analysis are reproduced by pure synthetic noise and are not real global degradations.
